note: The learner's mental structure. Module ids (F0-F5, 00-24) remain the engineering identity and are shown as secondary detail; this file is what the curriculum page is organised by.

entry.why: F0 is the reference demonstration, not a stage. It is deliberately outside the seven stages: a learner meets it before Stage 1 to acquire the problem, and every later stage refers back to it. Coverage checks treat it as entry rather than as an unmapped module.

stages.name: Understand AI
stages.question: What is this thing actually doing?
stages.plain: Before governance makes any sense, you need an accurate picture of what a model is and how it fails.

steps.name: What an AI model does
steps.plain: It predicts text. It does not look things up and it does not know things.

steps.name: Prompts and context
steps.plain: Everything the model can see arrives in one place — including text you did not write.

steps.name: Why output can be wrong
steps.plain: The same question can produce different answers, and confident ones can be false.

steps.name: Structured output and validation
steps.plain: Making the model's output checkable before anything uses it.

stages.name: From AI to agents
stages.question: When does an answer become an action?
stages.plain: The transition that creates the whole problem: software that can choose to do things.

steps.name: What a tool is
steps.plain: Your own function, handed to the model to call.

steps.name: What makes an agent
steps.plain: Choosing which tool to use, without a person in between.

steps.name: Side effects
steps.plain: The point where something real and possibly irreversible happens.

steps.name: Plans, loops and retries
steps.plain: Agents run in loops, and a retry can do the same thing twice.

steps.name: Multiple agents and handoffs
steps.plain: Work passed between agents can quietly gain authority on the way.

stages.name: Discover the governance problem
stages.question: Who decides, and where is it decided?
stages.plain: Each idea here answers a problem you have already watched happen.

steps.name: Wrong action versus wrong answer
steps.plain: Checking text is a different job from controlling behaviour.

steps.name: Identity
steps.plain: You cannot ask whether something is allowed without asking allowed for whom.

steps.name: Capability and authority
steps.plain: Declaring an action exists is not the same as granting it.

steps.name: Trust boundaries
steps.plain: Most harm is something crossing from inside to outside.

steps.name: Decisions
steps.plain: Getting an answer to "is this allowed?" — which by itself changes nothing.

steps.name: Enforcement
steps.plain: The place in your code that actually obeys the answer.

steps.name: Human approval
steps.plain: What it takes for "a human approved it" to mean anything.

stages.name: Prove what happened
stages.question: How would you know?
stages.plain: Turning a belief about your system into something you can show somebody.

steps.name: Attempts and completions
steps.plain: Two numbers that separate stopped, broken and done.

steps.name: Evidence
steps.plain: The record you point at instead of asserting.

steps.name: Integrity
steps.plain: Untampered is not the same as true.

steps.name: Locks and drift
steps.plain: Which version of the rules was actually in force.

steps.name: Assurance and its limits
steps.plain: How much weight your claim can carry, stated honestly.

steps.name: Bypass and coverage
steps.plain: The paths that are not guarded, and why they matter more than the ones that are.

stages.name: Learn Nornyx
stages.question: How do I express all of this in something checkable?
stages.plain: Only now does the tool itself make sense, because you know what it is for.

steps.name: What a .nyx contract is
steps.plain: The rules written down in a form a machine can check.

steps.name: Generate controls
steps.plain: Turning the contract into artifacts your system can use.

steps.name: Visual authoring
steps.plain: Building and checking a contract without writing it by hand.

steps.name: Authorization
steps.plain: Asking Nornyx for a decision from your own code.

steps.name: Runtime evidence
steps.plain: Recording what happened so the claim survives review.

steps.name: CI and conformance
steps.plain: Catching drift and broken enforcement before release.

stages.name: Framework integration
stages.question: How does this fit the tools I already use?
stages.plain: Real agent frameworks, with the coverage boundary stated each time.

steps.name: CrewAI
steps.plain: Placing the gate inside a crew's tool execution.

steps.name: LangGraph
steps.plain: Keeping occurrence identity straight across retries and loops.

steps.name: Multi-agent governance
steps.plain: Hierarchies, delegation and operations across several agents.

stages.name: Build it yourself
stages.question: Can you do it end to end?
stages.plain: Design, build, verify and audit a governed system without being walked through it.

steps.name: Capstone
steps.plain: The whole loop, on your own.
